free_tier.stated: 25 GB of storage, always free (does not expire), plus 25 WCU and 25 RCU provisioned capacity and ~200M requests/month

egress.terms: Metered — AWS gives 100 GB/month of data transfer out free, aggregated across all AWS services. 100 GB/month = ~3.3 GB/day vs 500 GB/day: 150x short. Beyond that, standard internet DTO rates.

tooling: AWS SDKs (boto3 etc.), `aws dynamodb` CLI, PartiQL; native `Binary` attribute type (raw bytes, base64 on the wire only); DynamoDB Streams + Lambda for processing
chaining: 25 GB per account per region, and the docs confirm 'the first 25 GB of storage are included in the AWS Free Tier in each AWS Region' — so N regions x 25 GB. 20 regions = 500 GB in principle, all under one account. This is the single largest structured-store byte allowance found. But the 25 RCU cap is region-global per table, so serving is throttled regardless.
limits_note: 400 KB max item (including attribute names); 25 RCU + 25 WCU provisioned; 100 bytes storage overhead per item; 25 GB/region free; binary values must be base64-encoded for transport but are sized by raw bytes

identity_cost.detail: inferred from the category 'iaas'; the source record states no identity cost, so this is a class assumption, not evidence

reliability_note: The most durable and operationally boring store in the dossier — no expiry, no pause, no deletion. The catch is throughput: 25 RCU is 25 strongly-consistent 4 KB reads/sec, which is a hard ceiling no amount of sharding within the free tier escapes.
confidence_note: One page read moves it to documented.
